## RANGE values and functions
# Sources: BigQuery's range-functions examples, data-types#range_type and lexical#range_literals;
# its comparable data types notes on RANGE; conversion_functions#cast_as_range. A RANGE<DATE> is
# returned as "[start, end)", with UNBOUNDED for a missing bound, as the client libraries parse it.

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-12-31)'
=> "[2020-01-01, 2020-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2020-12-31)'
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2020-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[NULL, 2020-12-31)'
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2020-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)'
=> "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> null

SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-01', DATE '2022-12-31')
=> "[2022-12-01, 2022-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE(NULL, DATE '2022-12-31')
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2022-12-31)"

SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-10-01', NULL)
=> "[2022-10-01, UNBOUNDED)"

# The lower bound must be smaller than the upper bound; SAFE. returns NULL instead.
SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01')
=> error:

SELECT RANGE(DATE '2022-12-01', DATE '2022-12-01')
=> error:

SELECT SAFE.RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01')
=> null

SELECT IF(FALSE, RANGE(DATE '2022-12-31', DATE '2022-12-01'), NULL)
=> null

SELECT RANGE_START(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-12-01, 2022-12-31)')
=> "2022-12-01"

SELECT RANGE_START(RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2022-12-31)')
=> null

SELECT RANGE_START(CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> null

SELECT RANGE_END(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-12-01, 2022-12-31)')
=> "2022-12-31"

SELECT RANGE_END(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-12-01, UNBOUNDED)')
=> null

SELECT RANGE_END(CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> null

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2022-04-01, 2022-07-01)')
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2023-01-01, 2023-04-01)')
=> "false"

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', DATE '2022-04-01')
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE_CONTAINS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-01-01, 2023-01-01)', DATE '2023-04-01')
=> "false"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, 2022-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "[2022-02-01, 2022-04-15)"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "[2022-02-01, 2022-04-15)"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, UNBOUNDED)')
=> "[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>))
=> null

# Ranges that do not overlap are an error; SAFE. returns NULL instead.
SELECT RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> error:

SELECT SAFE.RANGE_INTERSECT(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> null

SELECT RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, 2022-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE<DATE> '[2020-02-01, 2020-09-01)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, 2022-04-15)')
=> "false"

SELECT RANGE_OVERLAPS(RANGE<DATE> '[2022-02-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2021-06-15, UNBOUNDED)')
=> "true"

# Ranges compare by their lower bounds, then by their upper bounds. A NULL lower bound sorts
# before the others, a NULL upper bound after them, and two NULL bounds are equal.
SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2020-01-01)' < RANGE<DATE> '[2019-01-01, 2020-01-01)'
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)' > RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2021-01-01)'
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2021-01-01)' < RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-02, 2020-01-03)'
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, UNBOUNDED)' = RANGE(CAST(NULL AS DATE), NULL)
=> "true"

SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2021-01-01)' = CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> null

SELECT ARRAY(
  SELECT r FROM UNNEST([
    RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)', RANGE<DATE> '[2020-01-01, 2020-02-01)',
    RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01)']) AS r
  ORDER BY r)
=> [{"v": "[UNBOUNDED, 2021-01-01)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-01, 2020-02-01)"}, {"v": "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"}]

SELECT CAST('[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)' AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01, ', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[2020-01-01, 2020-01-02)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[UNBOUNDED, ', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2020-01-02)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01, ', 'NULL)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> "[2020-01-01, UNBOUNDED)"

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01, ', NULL) AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> null

# The text must have the range literal format.
SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-01,', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> error:

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('(2020-01-01, ', '2020-01-02)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> error:

SELECT CAST(CONCAT('[2020-01-02, ', '2020-01-01)') AS RANGE<DATE>)
=> error:
